questions.q: According to lesson 1, how do you strengthen your self-confidence?
a: Act and think like the person you want to be
Wait until success proves you right
Compare yourself with stronger competitors
Avoid situations that feel risky
questions.why: Lesson 1 says to build a powerful self-image by acting like your ideal self.

questions.q: What does the summary say about your performance and your self-image?
a: You can't long outperform the image you hold of yourself
Performance is unrelated to how you see yourself
A poor self-image helps you work harder
Only talent decides how far you get
questions.why: Lesson 1 states you can't underperform or outperform your self-image in the long run.

questions.q: What should your goals be built around, per lesson 2?
a: Your passion and who you want to become
Money and social status
What your peers expect of you
The easiest wins available
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to set goals out of passion, not money or status.

questions.q: What happens if you chase goals only for money or status you don't truly want?
a: You end up unfulfilled and miserable
You build mental toughness faster
You reach them with less effort
You gain extra confidence
questions.why: The summary warns that such achievements leave you unfulfilled.

questions.q: What does lesson 3 say produces success?
a: Gradual, steady improvement
Sudden bursts of motivation
One big overnight overhaul
Waiting for the right mood
questions.why: Lesson 3 says progressive effort beats occasional motivation.
